claims.claim: FineWeb-Edu used Llama3-70B-Instruct to generate 0–5 educational-value labels for 500,000 FineWeb samples, explicitly defining the target around grade-school and middle-school knowledge.
claims.notes: This is a concrete annotation protocol, not a universal rubric for all domains.

claims.claim: FineWeb-Edu observed that Mixtral-8x-7B tended to give more generous scores than Llama3-70B and Mixtral-8x22B; averaging the three model scores shifted the score distribution to the right.
claims.locator: Dataset curation → Annotation, model comparison and jury experiment
claims.notes: The dataset authors report their own experiment and hypothesize why jury-based annotations performed worse; do not generalize to every model jury.

claims.claim: FineWeb-Edu reports that a classifier trained on jury annotations performed worse in its filtering ablation than one trained on Llama3-only annotations.
claims.notes: The authors hypothesize the jury retained more low-quality samples; this explanation is not established as a universal causal mechanism.

claims.claim: MT-Bench / Chatbot Arena research documents position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases as limitations of LLM-as-a-judge.
claims.notes: Bias severity depends on task, judge, prompt and evaluation protocol.

claims.claim: A 2026 AACL survey of 665 NLP papers finds Cohen's kappa is frequently used regardless of whether its assumptions fit the task, while ICC is rarely reported for continuous-scale tasks; fewer than 5% of surveyed papers report confidence intervals.
claims.locator: Abstract; survey of 665 ACL Anthology papers and full-text analysis of 549 papers
claims.notes: These are descriptive statistics about the surveyed ACL Anthology corpus, not a claim about all NLP publications.

claims.claim: Cohen's kappa adjusts observed agreement by the agreement expected by chance: κ=(p_o−p_e)/(1−p_e).
claims.locator: Cohen (1960), A coefficient of agreement for nominal scales, definition of kappa
claims.notes: For ordinal labels use an appropriate weighted variant; multi-rater or continuous settings may require different statistics.

claims.claim: A reproducible LLM annotation protocol should version the rubric, prompt, judge model, sampling strategy and adjudication rules, then compare LLM-human agreement against a human-human baseline.
claims.locator: Twenty-Five Years of Inter-Annotator Agreement in NLP, abstract and reporting-practice findings
claims.notes: This is a process recommendation based on the paper's emphasis on agreement metric choice and reporting comparability.
